title: Stabiliser Box Upper Panel — Splice Region Crack Repair at Rib 6
abstract: Interim repair for a short crack at the rib 6 splice of the stabiliser box upper panel, with different acceptance and inspection intervals for the delivered and the extended stiffener standards.

sections.purpose: This repair covers a short crack found at the rib 6 splice of the upper panel during the scheduled detailed inspection, and returns the stabiliser to service for a defined interval pending a shop repair.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the crack length by eddy current and confirm it with a dye penetrant check after the sealant has been removed. The repair admits a single crack up to 18 millimetres long on the delivered stiffener standard and up to 25 millimetres on the extended standard, in either case not breaking into a fastener hole and not closer than 12 millimetres to the panel edge. Two cracks in the same bay, or any crack that reaches a fastener hole, are outside this repair. Record the crack position relative to rib six on the mapping sheet, because the shop repair scheme depends on which side of the splice the crack lies.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the sealant locally and clean the area. Stop drill each crack tip with the 4.8 millimetre drill and ream to the finished size, keeping the drill normal to the surface. Cold work each stop hole with the mandrel set to the specification. Install the splice plate over the cracked region, using the existing fastener rows where they align and the additional row shown on the repair drawing where they do not. Where the extended stiffener standard is fitted, use the thicker splice plate and the two row pattern; on the delivered standard use the shear tie item and the single row pattern. Install the fasteners wet with the faying surface sealant, working outward from the crack. Restore the protection scheme and reseal the region continuously.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an eddy current inspection of the repair region and both fastener rows at installation and record the baseline. Repeat at 1 500 flight cycles and then every 1 000 flight cycles until the shop repair is embodied. Do a detailed visual inspection at every C check. The repair is valid for 6 000 flight cycles from installation and must not be extended without a repair approval request.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: One crack up to 18 mm on the delivered stiffener standard, up to 25 mm on the extended standard, not breaking into a fastener hole and not closer than 12 mm to the panel edge.

materials.description: SHEAR TIE, STABILIZER BOX STRUCTURE, SUB-ASSY

type_data.fastener_pattern: Single row at 20 mm pitch on the delivered standard, two rows at 22 mm pitch on the extended standard, 15 mm edge distance
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Valid for 6 000 flight cycles from installation, with eddy current at 1 500 cycles and every 1 000 cycles after that. A shop repair is required before the limit.

issue.reason: Removal of the repair and assessment of its holes written in as a condition of embodying the extended stiffener standard, which occupies the same fastener rows.

abstract: Interim repair for a short crack at the rib 6 splice of the stabiliser box upper panel, with different acceptance and inspection intervals for the delivered and the extended stiffener standards, and the removal condition that applies before the extended standard is embodied.

sections.purpose: This repair covers a short crack found at the rib 6 splice of the upper panel during the scheduled detailed inspection, and returns the stabiliser to service for a defined interval pending a shop repair.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the crack length by eddy current and confirm it with a dye penetrant check after the sealant has been removed. The repair admits a single crack up to 18 millimetres long on the delivered stiffener standard and up to 25 millimetres on the extended standard, in either case not breaking into a fastener hole and not closer than 12 millimetres to the panel edge. Install the fasteners wet with the faying surface sealant, working outward from the crack. Restore the protection scheme and reseal the region continuously. Record the repair on the mapping sheet and flag it to the operator's modification planning: this repair sits on the fastener rows that the extended stiffener standard of MOD-168104 uses, and an aircraft carrying it cannot be taken straight into that embodiment.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an eddy current inspection of the repair region and both fastener rows at installation and record the baseline. Repeat at 1 500 flight cycles and then every 1 000 flight cycles until the shop repair is embodied. Do a detailed visual inspection at every C check. Removal before modification: this repair must be taken off before the extended stiffener standard is embodied, and it is not sufficient to install the modification over it. Remove the splice plate or shear tie, remove the sealant from the faying surfaces and do an eddy current and dye penetrant inspection of every hole the repair used, including both stop holes, before any new hole is drilled. Holes that are found sound are reamed to the oversize dimension of the modification; a hole with an indication, or a stop hole that has grown since the baseline, is a repair approval request and not a shop decision. Plan the removal into the same shop visit as the modification, because the panel is only open once.
